column1: # The device table of the Metal backend: how large each card is, how the backend schedules work on it, and which
# timing probes work on it.
# A line that is exactly [name] starts a section; the next row is that section's header and is required as written.
# Cells are separated by one tab. No file is read at run time: the generator below runs when CMake configures.
# [devices]: one row per card. device/gen-devices.cmake compiles the rows in (device-rows.h); device/init.m reads the
# row of the card it runs on (ggml_metal_device_row_of): a written cell sets the value, a - leaves it not known (sizes)
# or off (switches). A card with no row has no sizes, every switch off, one command buffer; rules that read a size
# (the matvec cache rule reads l1_bytes_per_cu) then run their setting for an unmeasured card.
# To add a card: run any prompt on it, copy its name from the log, write the cells you measured and - for the rest, and
# say in evidence where each cell comes from (specification, measurement, estimate).
# In the on | off | - columns, - leaves the switch as it is without a row (off).
#   card: the card's name as Metal reports it, exactly: the text after "found device: " in the log of any run on that card
#       (for example: AMD Radeon Pro Vega 64). A name that differs by one character matches no card. At most 62 bytes. One row per card.
#   chip: the chip's name for the reader, printed in the log. Free text, no tab, or -.
#   architecture: the family of [families] the card belongs to (for example gcn1, gcn5, rdna1), or -.
#   wave: threads of one wave on the card, as measured (the log line "probed simd_width"), or -. For the reader: the backend probes the width itself.
#   group_bytes: bytes of threadgroup memory the card allows (MTLDevice maxThreadgroupMemoryLength), or -. For the reader: the backend asks the device.
#   cu: compute units, a number above 0, or - = not known.
#   l1_bytes_per_cu: level-1 cache per compute unit in bytes, or - = not known.
#   l2_bytes: level-2 cache in bytes, or - = not known.
#   local_Bps: memory bandwidth of the card in bytes per second, or - = not known.
#   transfer_Bps: host to card transfer bandwidth in bytes per second, or - = not known.
#   attn_gate_fuse: on | off | -. on = the attention gate's copy, sigmoid, copy and multiply run as one launch.
#   conv_l2_fold: on | off | -. on = the conv_state launch also writes the split_l2 norms of its q and k heads.
#   add_norm_fuse: on | off | -. on = a residual add, the rms norm of its sum and the weight multiply run as one launch.
#   cb_seq: command buffers after the first, encoded and committed in order on the calling thread: 0 to 8, or - = one buffer encoded as without a row.
#   set_nowait: on | off | -. on = each input upload to a discrete card is committed without waiting for it.
#   staging_keep: on | off | -. on = one logits staging buffer is kept per context and reused every token.
#   probe_dispatch: on | off | -. Counter sampling at dispatch boundaries worked on the card (probe builds only).
#   probe_stage: on | off | -. Counter sampling at stage boundaries worked (probe builds only).
#   probe_blit: on | off | -. Counter sampling at blit boundaries worked. For the reader: no code reads it.
#   probe_timestamp: on | off | -. The timestamp counter worked. A probe build samples only on a card whose row says on here.
#   evidence: where each cell or group of cells comes from: specification, measurement (with its numbers) or estimate. Free text, no tab.
# [families]: one row per family of cards. A card is a member when its [devices] row names the family in architecture, or,
# when it has no row or its row's architecture is -, when Metal reports the family's metal_name for it; and only while the

# vendor the backend detected is the family's and the card reports the family's wave and group_bytes. A family has no settings of its own: rows keyed family:<name> in data/matmul.tsv are copies of a measured
# member's rows, the candidates a sweep tries first on another member (ggml_metal_family_row_of, device-rows.h).
#   family: the family's name: lower-case letters and digits (for example gcn1). One row per family.
#   vendor: amd | apple | intel | nvidia.
#   metal_name: the architecture name Metal reports for the family's cards (MTLDevice.architecture.name, macOS 14 and later), or - = not known. Two families never share a name.
# [launches]: the launch numbers of the kernels that have no table of their own: how many threads a threadgroup starts
# with, the amount of work up to which it grows, the most threads it takes, simdgroups and work units per threadgroup,
# threadgroup memory. device/gen-launches.cmake compiles the rows in (launch-ids.h: one id per launch, launch-rows.h);
# ggml_metal_launch_pick (device/launch-plan.cpp) gives the numbers of one launch on the card it runs on, in this order,
# a later row's cell that is not - replacing the earlier value:
#   1. the launch's default row: card any, wave any. Exactly one per launch, before its other rows; it writes every
#      cell the launch reads and - in the others. A card without a row runs it.
#   2. the launch's row of the card's wave: card any, wave a number. At most one per wave.
#   3. the card's own row: card = its Metal device name, wave = the wave it reports. Used only while the card reports
#      that wave. At most one per card and wave.
# The arithmetic that uses a number stays in the launch's code (what is doubled, what is capped); a row changes the
# number only. A row never lifts a limit: every launch still holds its threads to the compiled kernel's limit.
# In [launches], card and wave are the row's key as above, and evidence says where each written cell comes from.
# To change a number for a card: measure the op on the card with and without it, same output, and add the card's row.
# To give a launch its numbers here: add its default row with the numbers its code holds, its lines in
# device/launch-rules.cmake, then read them there.
# device/launch-rules.cmake holds, per launch, the cells it reads and the values its code runs; the generator refuses a
# default row that leaves a read cell -, a cell the launch does not read and a value outside the rule (to widen a rule,
# see that file's header).
# The launches and the cells each one reads (a cell not named is -):
#     l2_norm: start = threads of a threadgroup before it doubles up to the row length; mem_units = threadgroup memory.
#     group_norm: start = threads of a threadgroup (it does not grow); mem_units = threadgroup memory.

#     norm: the norm and rms_norm launches, plain and fused with multiply and add. start = threads before they double up to the row length; mem_units = threadgroup memory (one unit per thread the launch may take).
#     concat: start = a row of fewer storage units than this is packed with others into one threadgroup; cap = threads of a threadgroup otherwise.
#     concat_packed: cap = threads of a threadgroup of packed rows.
#     unary, glu, binary, conv_2d, cpy, act_copy (the activation copy), small_gate (the fused attention gate): cap = the most threads of a threadgroup.
#     rope, pad, pad_reflect_1d, arange, timestep_embedding: cap = the most threads of a threadgroup.
#     set_rows, tri: start = threads of a threadgroup before it doubles up to the row length.
#     diag: start = threads of a threadgroup (it does not grow).
#     soft_max: start = threads of a threadgroup before it doubles; work_min = it doubles while threads x rows is under this (and under the row length); mem_units = threadgroup memory.

#     ssm_conv_batch: the batched ssm_conv launch (more than one token). start = tokens per threadgroup for up to 4 tokens; cap = the most tokens per threadgroup (from 5 tokens: the smallest power of two from 8 that holds them, up to cap).

#     argmax: start = threads before they double; work_min = they double while threads x rows is under this; cap = threads of the entry that reads one aligned row as 4-float values; mem_units = threadgroup memory of both entries.
#     top_k_mask (its fill and its scatter), sum, sum_rows: start = threads of a threadgroup before they double.
#     cumsum: mem_units = threadgroup memory of the block pass.
#     count_equal: start = threads per simdgroup; nsg = the most simdgroups per threadgroup; mem_units = threadgroup memory.
#     argsort_merge (the merge pass of argsort and top_k): cap = the most threads of a threadgroup.
#     solve_tri: nsg = simdgroups per threadgroup.
#     ssm_scan: start = threads per simdgroup the launch counts its simdgroups by.
#     dsv4_hc (the head-combining launches): nsg = the most independent tokens or tiles packed into one threadgroup, one simdgroup each.
#     irfft, fold: cap = the most threads of a threadgroup.
#   launch: the launch's name: lower-case letters, digits and _ (for example rms_norm). Its id is GGML_METAL_LAUNCH_<NAME>.
#   start: threads of a threadgroup before it grows: a number, wave (the card's wave), or - = the launch has no start.
#   work_min: the amount of work (in the launch's own unit: threads x rows, or elements) up to which the threadgroup grows, or -.
#   cap: the most threads of a threadgroup the launch asks for, or - = only the compiled kernel's limit.
#   nsg: simdgroups per threadgroup, or -.
#   units: work units per threadgroup (rows, tokens, members: the launch's own unit), or -.
#   mem_units: threadgroup memory in 4-byte units: a number, wave (one unit per thread of a wave), or -.
